title: AMR pairing failure with abnormal fleet roster or mapping state
user_facing_summary: Use this path when a site reports that an ACB or zone cannot obtain an AMR pair, multiple AMRs route unexpectedly, or the system appears down after an AMR replacement or add/remove event.
playbook_goal: Determine whether the pairing failure is associated with an abnormal AMR roster or mapping state, use an authorized site-side isolation or removal procedure when supported, and confirm that normal pairing and operation return.
observed_entry_symptoms: A site reports that an ACB or affected zone cannot get a pair.
The ACB system is described as down or production is seriously impacted.
Replacement AMRs reportedly route to the hospital lane instead of supporting the affected workflow.
An AMR was previously reported with low battery or in an abnormal physical location.
The issue follows an AMR replacement, add, or remove activity.
negative_or_absent_signals: The source does not independently establish that low battery was the current cause.
The source does not provide readable RMS status values or a confirmed error code.
The source does not independently validate recovery through live telemetry.
No authoritative site location metadata was supplied in source_package.site_location.
support_user_language_examples: AMRs are going to the hospital
The robot was replaced and nothing is pairing
AGV was added but it is not getting a task
Robots are not working after an add/remove
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible abnormal AMR roster or mapping state after add/remove activity
Possible robot-location or pairing inconsistency affecting task assignment
Possible residual abnormal state after an earlier low-battery or physically inaccessible AMR event
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns from support discussion and case resolution text. The source supports a possible relationship between add/remove or mapping state and pairing failure, but it does not prove root cause or establish a reusable diagnosis.
confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom, a named RMS surface, discussion of possible roster/add-remove behavior, a source-supported site removal action, and reported recovery. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, recovery was reported rather than independently measured, and the source contains inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable pairing and routing pattern
nodes.intent: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records site-reported inability to get a pair, replacement AMRs going to the hospital lane, and earlier low-battery and robot-location circumstances.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support confirms through site interview or visual observation whether the affected zone cannot obtain a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the intended workflow, and whether the pattern followed an AMR replacement or add/remove event. Healthy means pairing and intended routing are available; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable or multiple AMRs show the reported abnormal routing; inconclusive means the site cannot confirm the affected workflow, timing, or current behavior.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages record a phone conversation with the site and site-reported pairing, low-battery, replacement, and hospital-lane behavior (case_228723:page_1; case_228723:page_2).

ontology_capabilities.support_contract: Confirm robot roster, mapping, locations, cell codes, or abnormal fleet membership.
ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes replacement/add activity, a robot reportedly not mapped, and abnormal routing.

ontology_gaps: No ontology-backed source mapping is provided for interpreting the phrase 'unable to get a pair' from the site interview alone.
healthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
AMRs are routing to the intended workflow rather than uniformly to the hospital lane.
unhealthy_indicators: Site confirms the affected zone still cannot obtain a pair.

A recent add/remove or replacement event coincides with the current failure.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot reproduce the pairing failure.
The affected workflow or current robot behavior cannot be identified.

nodes.title: Check fleet roster and mapping state
nodes.intent: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.goal: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source identifies RMS as the system used to view robot status and states that a removed robot was shown as not mapped; the artifact shows red-highlighted RMS table entries.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support inspects the RMS fleet or robot status view. Healthy means the relevant robot membership, mapping, and status appear consistent with the intended operating area; unhealthy means a robot is shown as not mapped, missing, duplicated, abnormal, or highlighted as an exception; inconclusive means the RMS view is unreadable, unavailable, or does not identify the relevant robot state.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet includes readable context identifying RMS screenshots and an artifact showing RMS robot status tables with red-highlighted entries (case_228723:page_6).

ontology_capabilities.support_contract: Confirm robot roster, mapping, locations, cell codes, or abnormal fleet membership.

healthy_indicators: RMS shows the relevant robot roster and mapping as consistent with the operating area.

nodes.title: Use an authorized site-side robot isolation or removal path
nodes.intent: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.goal: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident reports site-side removal of a robot from the system and placement on a charger, followed by reported system recovery.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site operator observes that the identified robot has been removed or isolated from active operation and placed in the reported safe state, such as charging, without creating a new physical hazard. Successful completion is confirmed by the site; failure or uncertainty means the robot cannot be safely isolated, the system-side state is unclear, or the action is outside the executor's authorization.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source includes RMS screenshots and a visible note that the site removed a robot from the system (case_228723:page_6).

ontology_gaps: The packet does not specify the approved remove/add procedure, authorization boundary, or exact system-side confirmation criteria.
healthy_indicators: Authorized site personnel confirm the affected robot is safely isolated and no longer participating in active operation.
unhealthy_indicators: The robot remains active, obstructed, or associated with the abnormal roster state.
The system continues to exhibit the pairing failure after the supported isolation action.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot confirm the robot's physical state or the corresponding RMS state.
The source-supported action cannot be performed safely or by an authorized role.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if physical access, safety conditions, authorization, or system-side state cannot be confirmed.

nodes.title: Confirm pairing and operational stability
nodes.intent: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the system began functioning after robot removal and remained operational during approximately ten minutes of monitoring, while acknowledging that the recovery was not independently validated by readable RMS data.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that the affected workflow can obtain a pair and that AMRs are operating as expected; where available, the operator or L1 support checks the RMS fleet view for the abnormal entry to be absent or no longer active. Healthy means pairing resumes and operation remains stable during observation; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue routing abnormally, or the abnormal RMS state persists; inconclusive means recovery is only reported administratively or the RMS details cannot be read.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports that the site believed the system was working and that support remained on the call to monitor it (case_228723:page_7).
The recovery evidence includes embedded RMS screenshots associated with the report that the system remained operational (case_228723:page_10).

extraction_notes: Exactly one candidate was produced for the incident packet.
source_package.site_location is empty; no ingestion site, site_code, or site_label was populated from that metadata.
The canonical record identifies UPS Fort Worth, TX (Haslet), but this candidate does not place that incident-specific site name in reusable node fields.
The source alternates between ACB and ECB naming; this ambiguity is preserved rather than resolved.
RMS screenshots contain unreadable or garbled details. Red entries are treated only as possible exception indicators.
The source supports a tentative roster or mapping pattern and a reported recovery after robot removal, not a confirmed root cause.
No ontology-backed WCS SQL, API, service, or database evidence was used because those surfaces were not established by the incident evidence as the historical troubleshooting surface.
The later CBRE work-order artifact and case-management history were excluded from the technical path.
summary: Use this path when a site reports that an ACB or zone cannot obtain an AMR pair, multiple AMRs route unexpectedly, or the system appears down after an AMR replacement or add/remove event.
